brief.destination: CallerSignal behaves like a trustworthy HIBP-style caller-campaign intelligence service: one search yields a calibrated answer, campaign history, concrete actions, private monitoring, verified organisation context, transparent corpus coverage, and an agent-native remote MCP surface.
brief.problem: CallerSignal has a strong read-only lookup and risk presentation, but most results still expose numbering context rather than risk-capable campaign evidence, and the product lacks the recurring value loops, verified ownership workflows, public corpus transparency, and hosted agent access that make HIBP useful beyond a one-off search.
brief.chosen_approach: Make CallerSignal a HIBP-like caller-campaign intelligence service: model campaigns as the durable risk object; collect only structured first-party reports under privacy and moderation controls; add private watch notifications and verified organisation number portfolios; publish consumer campaign transparency and a hosted OAuth-aware MCP surface; keep source-rights, spoofing, no-safe-number, and no-lookup-popularity invariants.
non_goals: Scrape, copy, or derive reputation from unlicensed third-party caller-report databases.
Publish free-text accusations, requester identities, raw call histories, lookup trails, or real phone-number fixtures in Git.
Treat a displayed number, number ownership claim, lookup volume, or one unverified report as proof of caller identity, guilt, or safety.
Ship live outbound notifications, persistent personal data, or authentication against an undeclared provider or without explicit retention, deletion, abuse, and incident controls.
Turn the public consumer UI into an alternative source of truth distinct from CLI, MCP, and HTTP contracts.

source.recommendation: Make CallerSignal a HIBP-like caller-campaign intelligence service: model campaigns as the durable risk object; collect only structured first-party reports under privacy and moderation controls; add private watch notifications and verified organisation number portfolios; publish consumer campaign transparency and a hosted OAuth-aware MCP surface; keep source-rights, spoofing, no-safe-number, and no-lookup-popularity invariants.

work_units.summary: Define caller campaigns as the durable risk-intelligence object
acceptance: A versioned campaign contract records status, categories, jurisdictions, first/last seen, eligible evidence, confidence, freshness, recommended actions, and correction state without asserting caller or subscriber identity.
Campaign membership refers only to calls displaying a number or matching a bounded pattern, remains spoofing-aware, and uses only synthetic reserved-number fixtures in repository tests.
Campaign lifecycle and evidence invariants are schema-valid, deterministic, and fail closed when evidence is stale, ineligible, contradictory, or insufficient.

work_units.summary: Create privacy-operable persistence and outbox boundaries
acceptance: Storage ports support atomic report, campaign, watch, verification-challenge, notification-outbox, correction, and deletion operations without retaining requester IPs or raw lookup histories.

A deterministic local adapter proves retention expiry, deduplication, deletion, audit receipts, and transactional outbox behavior while production provider configuration remains secret and replaceable.
The data map documents purpose, fields, lawful-basis review status, retention, access, encryption/key boundaries, incident handling, and the explicit provider gate for Vercel deployment.

work_units.summary: Add verified private watch subscriptions and change notifications
acceptance: A watch requires verified contact ownership, exposes no public subscriber data, minimizes stored number/contact material, and can be listed, revoked, expired, corrected, and deleted.
Notifications are generated only for material campaign or risk-state changes, are idempotent through an outbox, contain no accusation or hidden lookup trail, and preserve a no-safety caveat.
Rate limiting, anti-enumeration, consent receipts, delivery failure, provider outage, and unsubscribe behavior fail closed and are covered by deterministic tests.

work_units.summary: Verify organisations and publish bounded official-number portfolios
acceptance: Organisation control is verified through an explicit challenge workflow before a bounded number portfolio can be published, changed, or removed.
A verified portfolio proves only that the organisation declared an official contact route; it never proves that a call displaying that number originated from the organisation.
Challenges expire, replay fails, changes are audited, conflicts and impersonation reports fail closed, and correction/deletion/appeal paths are tested.

work_units.summary: Build the consumer campaign timeline and action experience
acceptance: The number replaces the generic result title and the first screen shows one calibrated state, coverage recency, a concrete safety checklist, campaign history, and clear report/watch actions while technical evidence is progressively disclosed.

A public campaign catalogue and detail route expose only eligible aggregated evidence, transparent status and dates, verified organisation context, corrections, and exact source coverage without displaying private reports or lookup popularity.

Mobile and desktop browser proof shows accessible text-and-icon semantics, no clipping, overlap, overflow, temporary copy, or console errors across empty, unknown, elevated, official-warning, and campaign-detail states.

work_units.summary: Publish honest corpus, coverage, and methodology transparency
acceptance: Public metrics are derived only from enabled sources, eligible campaigns, verified portfolios, and privacy-thresholded aggregates; lookup volume never becomes reputation evidence.

Coverage explicitly names jurisdictions, risk-capable sources, freshness, last successful ingest, unavailable gaps, moderation thresholds, correction counts, and methodology version without vanity or unsupported totals.
The README and website make corpus limitations and the meaning of no matching evidence immediately understandable.

work_units.summary: Expose CallerSignal through a discoverable hosted MCP service
acceptance: A hosted MCP endpoint publishes discovery metadata and read-only tools for number lookup, campaign research, source coverage, and methodology with the same canonical contracts as CLI and HTTP.

Protected watch and organisation tools require explicit OAuth scopes and consent, advertise accurate read-only/open-world/destructive hints, and cannot bypass verification, rate, privacy, or deletion controls.

Local protocol tests and live Vercel proof cover discovery, initialization, tool listing, representative public calls, unauthorized protected calls, no-store headers, privacy-safe errors, and production alias health.
